correctness.rationale: Each arm needs a selected interior by equal alternative terminal paths; strict depth-sum inequalities classify all size-(r+1) possibilities and rule out size r. Explicit unique-geodesic witness pairs establish feasibility. Symmetric-difference adjacency yields two punctured r-cubes and precisely r bridging two-edge paths, with exact edge counts and diameter proof. The separate BFS deletion-distance checker examined 873813 subsets in r=3..7 and independently checked every predicted minimum set and adjacency invariant. Enumeration is corroboration, not the proof for arbitrary r.

originality.rationale: Multiple actual semantic searches of mathematical research records and primary literature were compared by theorem implication rather than matching words. Same-network edge-general-position, Rips-theta topology, stronger geodetic covering, general subdivision inequalities and cyclomatic-number bounds do not imply the exact MEG minimizer families or reconfiguration network. No direct prior coverage identified; bibliographic incompleteness remains a material risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible source could already determine r-arm four-edge theta MEG optima or their token-jump graph; negative search is not proof of priority.
The closest exact graph-family comparison in accessible history concerns different edge-general-position quantifiers, so lack of implication has been reasoned rather than established by title.

value.rationale: The r-arm same-length parallel-path network is a natural failure-monitoring testbed with tied routes. Exact classifications of all optimal sensor locations, exponential optimum count, a complete feasible one-replacement graph and sharp linear diameter provide new structural and reconfiguration information beyond a minimum-size number. The theorem applies to every r>=3 and is not a routine one-parameter recomputation.
